> alacritty

see https://github.com/jwilm/alacritty/issues/736#issuecomment-323512752

Essentially: we trust terminfo, and xterm-256color on macOS is outdated. You can fix the issue by updating your terminfo.

@DarkDefender at `:help nvim-features-changed` I see that one of the changes from the TUI refactor was that we don't "fill in" missing terminfo entries from our builtin terminfos. I think we should do that, what do you think?

> Nvim uses either one or the other of an external terminfo entry or the built-in one.  It does not attempt to mix data from the two.

issue.title: Cursor no longer changing on macOS High Sierra (0.2.0 -> 0.2.1)

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
- `nvim --version`: 0.2.1 +
- nvim (version: ) behaves differently? 0.2.0 (`/usr/local/Cellar/neovim/0.2.1/bin/nvim`)
- Operating system/version: macOS High Sierra 
- Terminal name/version: `Terminal.app` (and `Alacritty`)
- `$TERM`: `xterm-256color`

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim -u NORC`

`nvim -u NORC`

### Actual behaviour

Cursor is what it was in the shell before running vim (usually I-bar).

### Expected behaviour

Cursor starts as a block (normal mode), and becomes an I-bar when you go into insert mode.

### Other info

`set guicursor` returns `guicursor=n-v-c-sm:block,i-ci-ve:ver25,r-cr-o:hor20` for both 0.2.0 and 0.2.1

I know there have been some changes here, so sorry if I just need to set something different now. 

I can't reproduce this on my Linux box, but I can reproduce by building from source on the latest master (30a21830d06f1e99431c2a632133577841b10c32).

body:
From within "Terminal.app" (ver2.8, macoSv10.13), the following executions can change
the shape of the cursor.

	$ echo -ne '\e[1 q'
	$ echo -ne '\e[2 q'
	$ echo -ne '\e[3 q'
	$ echo -ne '\e[4 q'
	$ echo -ne '\e[5 q'
	$ echo -ne '\e[6 q'
	$ echo -ne '\e[0 q'

>You can fix the issue by updating your terminfo.

The "macOS has a bad terminfo, you should update it" argument seems fair, but if this breaks everyone on macOS who isn't using iTerm, then a guide explaining how to fix this would be helpful. Especially as it's a regression from the previous release. Maybe something for the FAQ?

Copying the `terminfo` from @DarkDefender (in https://github.com/jwilm/alacritty/issues/736#issuecomment-323512752) does fix the problem for me:

```bash
curl -sL -O https://github.com/jwilm/alacritty/files/1236221/xterm-256color.zip
unzip xterm-256color.zip; rm xterm-256color.zip
cp ~/.terminfo/78/xterm-256color ~/.terminfo/78/xterm-256color.bak
mv xterm-256color ~/.terminfo/78/xterm-256color
```

**_EDIT:_** You can also just do `alias nvim="TERM=tmux-256color nvim"`
@gibfahn This is definitely a  regression, it'll be fixed.
